Derivations by chapter

Worked, typeset derivations across all six prescribed chapters.

How to earn derivation marks

Write the diagram or geometry, symmetry/assumptions, defining equation, algebra and boxed final result. Do not memorise an unexplained last line. A full-board PYQ is not a guaranteed half-yearly question.

Coulomb force in vector form

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 14–15

For charges at position vectors, write separation and its unit vector.

r12=r1−r2\mathbf r_{12}=\mathbf r_1-\mathbf r_2r12​=r1​−r2​
r^12=r12/r12\hat{\mathbf r}_{12}=\mathbf r_{12}/r_{12}r^12​=r12​/r12​

Apply inverse-square Coulomb law.

F12=q1q24πε0r122r^12\mathbf F_{12}=\dfrac{q_1q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{12}^{2}}\hat{\mathbf r}_{12}F12​=4πε0​r122​q1​q2​​r^12​

Result

F12=q1q24πε0r12r123\mathbf F_{12}=\dfrac{q_1q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{\mathbf r_{12}}{r_{12}^{3}}F12​=4πε0​q1​q2​​r123​r12​​

STATED THEN REWRITTEN: Empirical law, not a first-principles derivation; point charges at rest in vacuum.

Superposition of electrostatic forces

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 19–20

Apply Coulomb law separately to every source charge.

F1i=q1qi4πε0r1i2r^1i\mathbf F_{1i}=\dfrac{q_1q_i}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{1i}^{2}}\hat{\mathbf r}_{1i}F1i​=4πε0​r1i2​q1​qi​​r^1i​

Vector-add contributions.

F1=F12+F13+⋯+F1n\mathbf F_1=\mathbf F_{12}+\mathbf F_{13}+\cdots+\mathbf F_{1n}F1​=F12​+F13​+⋯+F1n​

Result

F1=q14πε0∑i=2nqir^1ir1i2\mathbf F_1=\dfrac{q_1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{i=2}^{n}\dfrac{q_i\hat{\mathbf r}_{1i}}{r_{1i}^{2}}F1​=4πε0​q1​​∑i=2n​r1i2​qi​r^1i​​

Superposition itself is experimentally verified, not proved from Coulomb law alone; NCERT Eq. 1.5.

Electric field of a point charge

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 22–23

Divide Coulomb force on a test charge by that charge.

F=Qq4πε0r2r^\mathbf F=\dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^{2}}\hat{\mathbf r}F=4πε0​r2Qq​r^
E=lim⁡q→0Fq\mathbf E=\lim_{q\to0}\dfrac{\mathbf F}{q}E=limq→0​qF​

Result

E=Q4πε0r2r^\mathbf E=\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^{2}}\hat{\mathbf r}E=4πε0​r2Q​r^

For an ideal point source and undisturbing test charge; field points inward for Q<0.

Field due to several point charges

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 23–24

Find each individual field at observation point P.

Ei=qi4πε0riP2r^iP\mathbf E_i=\dfrac{q_i}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{iP}^{2}}\hat{\mathbf r}_{iP}Ei​=4πε0​riP2​qi​​r^iP​

Use vector superposition.

E(P)=E1+⋯+En\mathbf E(P)=\mathbf E_1+\cdots+\mathbf E_nE(P)=E1​+⋯+En​

Result

E(P)=14πε0∑i=1nqir^iPriP2\mathbf E(P)=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\dfrac{q_i\hat{\mathbf r}_{iP}}{r_{iP}^{2}}E(P)=4πε0​1​∑i=1n​riP2​qi​r^iP​​

Do not add field magnitudes unless collinear; NCERT Eq. 1.10.

Electric flux through a plane and curved surface

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 29–31

Project area onto plane normal to field.

Δϕ=E ΔScos⁡θ=E⋅ΔS\Delta\phi=E\,\Delta S\cos\theta=\mathbf E\cdot\Delta\mathbf SΔϕ=EΔScosθ=E⋅ΔS

Sum infinitesimal surface elements.

ϕ≃∑iEi⋅ΔSi\phi\simeq\sum_i\mathbf E_i\cdot\Delta\mathbf S_iϕ≃∑i​Ei​⋅ΔSi​

Result

ϕ=∫SE⋅dS\phi=\int_S\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf Sϕ=∫S​E⋅dS

For a closed surface normals point outward; textbook gives limiting sum and mentions integral, not a separate integral derivation.

Electric field on dipole axis

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 31–32

At axial distance r from centre on positive-charge side, subtract opposing fields.

E=q4πε0[1(r−a)2−1(r+a)2]p^\mathbf E=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\dfrac{1}{(r-a)^2}-\dfrac{1}{(r+a)^2}\right]\hat{\mathbf p}E=4πε0​q​[(r−a)21​−(r+a)21​]p^​

Combine fractions and put p=2qa.

E=4qar4πε0(r2−a2)2p^=2pr4πε0(r2−a2)2p^\mathbf E=\dfrac{4qar}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2-a^2)^2}\hat{\mathbf p}=\dfrac{2pr}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2-a^2)^2}\hat{\mathbf p}E=4πε0​(r2−a2)24qar​p^​=4πε0​(r2−a2)22pr​p^​

Neglect a² against r² for far field.

E≃2p4πε0r3p^\mathbf E\simeq\dfrac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\hat{\mathbf p}E≃4πε0​r32p​p^​

Result

Eaxial=2pr4πε0(r2−a2)2p^(r>a)\mathbf E_{\rm axial}=\dfrac{2pr}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2-a^2)^2}\hat{\mathbf p}\quad(r>a)Eaxial​=4πε0​(r2−a2)22pr​p^​(r>a)

Far-field form requires r≫a; exact expression given for r>a on positive side. Point-dipole limit exact for r>0.

Electric field on dipole equatorial plane

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 31–32

Equal charge-field magnitudes have cancelling transverse components; axial components reinforce opposite p.

E+=E−=q4πε0(r2+a2)E_+=E_-=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2+a^2)}E+​=E−​=4πε0​(r2+a2)q​
cos⁡θ=ar2+a2\cos\theta=\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{r^2+a^2}}cosθ=r2+a2​a​

Resolve components and substitute p=2qa.

E=−2E+cos⁡θ p^=−p4πε0(r2+a2)3/2p^\mathbf E=-2E_+\cos\theta\,\hat{\mathbf p}=-\dfrac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}}\hat{\mathbf p}E=−2E+​cosθp^​=−4πε0​(r2+a2)3/2p​p^​

Take r≫a.

E≃−p4πε0r3p^\mathbf E\simeq-\dfrac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\hat{\mathbf p}E≃−4πε0​r3p​p^​

Result

Eequatorial=−p4πε0(r2+a2)3/2p^\mathbf E_{\rm equatorial}=-\dfrac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}}\hat{\mathbf p}Eequatorial​=−4πε0​(r2+a2)3/2p​p^​

Far-field expression requires r≫a; point-dipole limit exact outside origin.

Torque on dipole in uniform electric field

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 35

Forces ±qE cancel as a net force but form a couple of arm 2a sinθ.

Fnet=0F_{\rm net}=0Fnet​=0
τ=qE(2asin⁡θ)=pEsin⁡θ\tau=qE(2a\sin\theta)=pE\sin\thetaτ=qE(2asinθ)=pEsinθ

Use right-hand-rule direction.

τ=p×E\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf p\times\mathbf Eτ=p×E

Result

τ=p×E\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf p\times\mathbf Eτ=p×E

Permanent dipole and spatially uniform E; nonuniform field can exert net force.

Field of a continuous volume charge distribution

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 36–37

Replace small volume element by charge ρΔV and apply Coulomb law.

Δq=ρ(r)ΔV\Delta q=\rho(\mathbf r)\Delta VΔq=ρ(r)ΔV
ΔE=ρ(r)ΔV4πε0r′2r^′\Delta\mathbf E=\dfrac{\rho(\mathbf r)\Delta V}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^{\prime2}}\hat{\mathbf r}^{\prime}ΔE=4πε0​r′2ρ(r)ΔV​r^′

E(P)≃14πε0∑ρΔVr^′r′2\mathbf E(P)\simeq\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum\dfrac{\rho\Delta V\hat{\mathbf r}^{\prime}}{r^{\prime2}}E(P)≃4πε0​1​∑r′2ρΔVr^′​

Result

E(P)=14πε0∫ρ(r)r^′r′2 dV\mathbf E(P)=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int\dfrac{\rho(\mathbf r)\hat{\mathbf r}^{\prime}}{r^{\prime2}}\,dVE(P)=4πε0​1​∫r′2ρ(r)r^′​dV

NCERT Eq. 1.27 explicitly stops at approximate sum; integral is limiting notation, not evaluated.

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 37–38

E=q4πε0r2E=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}E=4πε0​r2q​
Δϕ=EΔS\Delta\phi=E\Delta SΔϕ=EΔS

ϕ=E∑ΔS=q4πε0r2(4πr2)\phi=E\sum\Delta S=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}(4\pi r^2)ϕ=E∑ΔS=4πε0​r2q​(4πr2)

ϕ=qε0\phi=\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}ϕ=ε0​q​

qenc=λLq_{\rm enc}=\lambda Lqenc​=λL

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 42–43

Pillbox of face area A has equal flux on both faces; sides contribute zero.

ϕ=2EA\phi=2EAϕ=2EA
qenc=σAq_{\rm enc}=\sigma Aqenc​=σA

2EA=σAε02EA=\dfrac{\sigma A}{\varepsilon_0}2EA=ε0​σA​

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 43–44

E(4πr2)=qε0E(4\pi r^2)=\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}E(4πr2)=ε0​q​
q=4πR2σq=4\pi R^2\sigmaq=4πR2σ

Electrostatic potential difference from work

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 56–57

The external force balances the electric force during quasistatic movement.

Fext=−qE\mathbf F_{\rm ext}=-q\mathbf EFext​=−qE
WR→P=∫RPFext⋅dℓ=−q∫RPE⋅dℓW_{R\to P}=\int_R^P\mathbf F_{\rm ext}\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell=-q\int_R^P\mathbf E\cdot d\boldsymbol\ellWR→P​=∫RP​Fext​⋅dℓ=−q∫RP​E⋅dℓ

Work changes potential energy; divide by test charge.

UP−UR=WR→PU_P-U_R=W_{R\to P}UP​−UR​=WR→P​
VP−VR=UP−URqV_P-V_R=\dfrac{U_P-U_R}{q}VP​−VR​=qUP​−UR​​

Result

VP−VR=−∫RPE⋅dℓV_P-V_R=-\int_R^P\mathbf E\cdot d\boldsymbol\ellVP​−VR​=−∫RP​E⋅dℓ

Potential reference is arbitrary; NCERT says proof of path-independence from Coulomb law is omitted.

Potential due to a point charge

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 57–58

External force per unit positive test charge opposes radial Coulomb field.

dW=−Q4πε0r′2 dr′dW=-\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^{\prime2}}\,dr^{\prime}dW=−4πε0​r′2Q​dr′

Integrate from infinity with V(∞)=0.

V(r)=∫∞r−Q4πε0r′2 dr′V(r)=\int_{\infty}^{r}-\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^{\prime2}}\,dr^{\prime}V(r)=∫∞r​−4πε0​r′2Q​dr′

Result

V(r)=Q4πε0rV(r)=\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r}V(r)=4πε0​rQ​

Point charge; holds for either sign Q; NCERT Eqs. 2.5–2.8.

Potential of an electric dipole

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 59–61

Add scalar potentials of ±q.

V=q4πε0(1r+−1r−)V=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac1{r_+}-\dfrac1{r_-}\right)V=4πε0​q​(r+​1​−r−​1​)
r±2=r2+a2∓2arcos⁡θr_\pm^2=r^2+a^2\mp2ar\cos\thetar±2​=r2+a2∓2arcosθ

For r≫a use first-order binomial approximation.

1r+≃1r(1+acos⁡θr)\dfrac1{r_+}\simeq\dfrac1r\left(1+\dfrac{a\cos\theta}{r}\right)r+​1​≃r1​(1+racosθ​)
1r−≃1r(1−acos⁡θr)\dfrac1{r_-}\simeq\dfrac1r\left(1-\dfrac{a\cos\theta}{r}\right)r−​1​≃r1​(1−racosθ​)

Insert p=2qa.

V≃pcos⁡θ4πε0r2V\simeq\dfrac{p\cos\theta}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}V≃4πε0​r2pcosθ​

Result

V(r)=p⋅r^4πε0r2V(\mathbf r)=\dfrac{\mathbf p\cdot\hat{\mathbf r}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}V(r)=4πε0​r2p⋅r^​

Approximate for finite dipole r≫a, exact for ideal point dipole; equatorial potential zero; axis ±p/(4πε₀r²).

Potential due to charge system and shell

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 61–62

Scalar potential superposes algebraically.

Vi(P)=qi4πε0riPV_i(P)=\dfrac{q_i}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{iP}}Vi​(P)=4πε0​riP​qi​​
V(P)=∑iVi(P)V(P)=\sum_iV_i(P)V(P)=∑i​Vi​(P)

For uniformly charged shell, external potential is point-charge potential; interior E=0 gives constant V matched at R.

V(r<R)=V(R)=q4πε0RV(r<R)=V(R)=\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0R}V(r<R)=V(R)=4πε0​Rq​

Result

V(P)=14πε0∑iqiriP;Vshell={q4πε0r,r≥Rq4πε0R,r<RV(P)=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_i\dfrac{q_i}{r_{iP}};\quad V_{\rm shell}=\begin{cases}\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r},&r\ge R\\\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0R},&r<R\end{cases}V(P)=4πε0​1​∑i​riP​qi​​;Vshell​=⎩⎨⎧​4πε0​rq​,4πε0​Rq​,​r≥Rr<R​

Potential sum for point charges; shell result assumes uniform surface charge. Continuous-charge integral mentioned but not performed.

Equipotentials perpendicular to electric field

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 64

A tangential E component would do nonzero work along equipotential, contradicting ΔV=0.

ΔW=qE⋅Δℓ\Delta W=q\mathbf E\cdot\Delta\boldsymbol\ellΔW=qE⋅Δℓ
ΔV=−ΔWq=0\Delta V=-\dfrac{\Delta W}{q}=0ΔV=−qΔW​=0

Result

E⋅dℓ=0along an equipotential\mathbf E\cdot d\boldsymbol\ell=0\quad\text{along an equipotential}E⋅dℓ=0along an equipotential

At points where E≠0, field is normal to equipotential surface.

Relation of electric field and potential

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 64–65

Move unit positive charge a small normal distance δl opposite field; external work equals potential difference.

Eδl=−δVE\delta l=-\delta VEδl=−δV

Take infinitesimal limit.

En=−dVdlE_n=-\dfrac{dV}{dl}En​=−dldV​

Result

E=−∇V\mathbf E=-\boldsymbol\nabla VE=−∇V

NCERT Eq. 2.20 explicitly gives E=−δV/δl normal to equipotentials; full vector gradient is equivalent extension, not separately derived there.

Potential energy of two and three point charges

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 65–66

First charge costs no work from infinity; second costs q₂ times first potential.

W1=0W_1=0W1​=0
W2=q2V1(r2)=q1q24πε0r12W_2=q_2V_1(\mathbf r_2)=\dfrac{q_1q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{12}}W2​=q2​V1​(r2​)=4πε0​r12​q1​q2​​

Third costs q₃ times potential of first two; add pair energies.

W3=14πε0(q1q3r13+q2q3r23)W_3=\dfrac1{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{q_1q_3}{r_{13}}+\dfrac{q_2q_3}{r_{23}}\right)W3​=4πε0​1​(r13​q1​q3​​+r23​q2​q3​​)

Result

U=14πε0∑i<jqiqjrijU=\dfrac1{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{i<j}\dfrac{q_iq_j}{r_{ij}}U=4πε0​1​∑i<j​rij​qi​qj​​

No self-energies; assemble from infinity, electrostatic forces conservative.

Potential energy of charges in external field

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 68–69

Bring first charge against external potential; bring second against external and first charge.

W1=q1Vext(r1)W_1=q_1V_{\rm ext}(\mathbf r_1)W1​=q1​Vext​(r1​)
W2=q2Vext(r2)+q1q24πε0r12W_2=q_2V_{\rm ext}(\mathbf r_2)+\dfrac{q_1q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{12}}W2​=q2​Vext​(r2​)+4πε0​r12​q1​q2​​

Result

U=q1Vext(r1)+q2Vext(r2)+q1q24πε0r12U=q_1V_{\rm ext}(\mathbf r_1)+q_2V_{\rm ext}(\mathbf r_2)+\dfrac{q_1q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r_{12}}U=q1​Vext​(r1​)+q2​Vext​(r2​)+4πε0​r12​q1​q2​​

External potential excludes field produced by charges being assembled; single charge U=qV_ext.

Potential energy of dipole in uniform external field

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 70–71

Quasistatically rotate against torque pE sinθ.

Wext=∫θ0θpEsin⁡ϑ dϑ=pE(cos⁡θ0−cos⁡θ)W_{\rm ext}=\int_{\theta_0}^{\theta}pE\sin\vartheta\,d\vartheta=pE(\cos\theta_0-\cos\theta)Wext​=∫θ0​θ​pEsinϑdϑ=pE(cosθ0​−cosθ)

Choose U=0 for θ₀=π/2.

U(θ)=−pEcos⁡θU(\theta)=-pE\cos\thetaU(θ)=−pEcosθ

Result

U=−p⋅EU=-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf EU=−p⋅E

Uniform external E, permanent dipole; interaction self-energy is independent of θ and dropped.

Einside=0\mathbf E_{\rm inside}=0Einside​=0

Einside=0,ρexcess,inside=0,Vconductor=constant\mathbf E_{\rm inside}=0,\quad \rho_{\rm excess,inside}=0,\quad V_{\rm conductor}=\text{constant}Einside​=0,ρexcess,inside​=0,Vconductor​=constant

Capacitance proportionality and definition

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 77–78

For fixed conductor geometry and dielectric, linear electrostatic fields scale with deposited plate charge.

Q↦kQ⟹E↦kE⟹V↦kVQ\mapsto kQ\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E\mapsto kE\quad\Longrightarrow\quad V\mapsto kVQ↦kQ⟹E↦kE⟹V↦kV

Their ratio therefore defines a geometry-dependent capacitance.

Q∝VQ\propto VQ∝V

Result

C=QVC=\dfrac QVC=VQ​

NCERT Eq. 2.38; assumes linear medium, plates carry +Q and −Q. This is a definition argued from proportionality, not an independent field calculation.

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 78–79

Superpose two sheet fields; outside cancels, inside adds.

σ=Q/A\sigma=Q/Aσ=Q/A
Ebetween=σ2ε0+σ2ε0=Qε0AE_{\rm between}=\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}+\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}=\dfrac{Q}{\varepsilon_0A}Ebetween​=2ε0​σ​+2ε0​σ​=ε0​AQ​

Uniform field gives voltage; use C=Q/V.

V=Ed=Qdε0AV=Ed=\dfrac{Qd}{\varepsilon_0A}V=Ed=ε0​AQd​
C=Q/VC=Q/VC=Q/V

Result

C0=ε0AdC_0=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}C0​=dε0​A​

Large plates, d²≪A; neglect fringing; NCERT Eqs. 2.39–2.43.

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 79–81

Polarization produces bound surface densities ±σp opposing free-charge field.

E=σ−σpε0E=\dfrac{\sigma-\sigma_p}{\varepsilon_0}E=ε0​σ−σp​​
σ−σp=σK\sigma-\sigma_p=\dfrac{\sigma}{K}σ−σp​=Kσ​

Compute reduced V at fixed free charge, then C.

V=Ed=QdKε0AV=Ed=\dfrac{Qd}{K\varepsilon_0A}V=Ed=Kε0​AQd​
C=Q/VC=Q/VC=Q/V

Result

C=Kε0Ad=KC0C=K\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}=KC_0C=Kdε0​A​=KC0​

Entire gap filled with homogeneous linear dielectric; K=ε/ε₀>1. P·n=σp on PDF p81 is TAKEN WITHOUT PROOF.

Polarisation surface charge and electric displacement

NCERT Part I PDF pp. 80–81

NCERT takes the surface bound-charge relation without proof.

σb=P⋅n^\sigma_{\rm b}=\mathbf P\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}σb​=P⋅n^

For parallel plates define displacement and relate to free surface charge.

D=ε0E+P\mathbf D=\varepsilon_0\mathbf E+\mathbf PD=ε0​E+P
